metadata.note: The answer to 'when was the first passenger rail to Richmond': 1836, the Richmond, Fredericksburg and Potomac Railroad's initial segment from Richmond to Hazel Run (just south of Fredericksburg). Virginia's actual first railroad was earlier still -- the 1831 Chesterfield Railroad, a gravity-and-mule-powered coal line from the Midlothian mines to the James River -- but that was freight-only, not scheduled passenger service, and didn't reach Richmond proper. The RF&P is also notable for surviving essentially intact into the present: it's now CSX's RF&P Subdivision, and Amtrak still runs multiple daily trains over this exact corridor (Northeast Regional, Carolinian, Palmetto, Silver Meteor, Silver Star -- see amtrak.geojson, though that file's Northeast Regional entry only covers DC-Boston, not this Richmond-DC extension). Geometry is real-traced from OpenStreetMap active-rail geometry for the entire Richmond-Washington corridor -- connected cleanly with no gaps, unsurprising given how heavily used this line still is today.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond,_Fredericksburg_and_Potomac_Railroad (chartered Feb 25 1834; Richmond-Hazel Run opened 1836, the earliest regular passenger/freight service from Richmond; Richmond-Fredericksburg complete Jan 23 1837; extended to Aquia Creek Sep 30 1842, connecting to Washington DC via the company's own steamboat line; separate companies -- Alexandria & Washington RR 1857, Alexandria & Fredericksburg Railway reaching Quantico 1872 -- provided the DC-Quantico rail link, merging into the Washington Southern Railway in 1890, which formally merged into the RF&P Feb 24 1920, finally unifying Richmond-DC under one rail company; RF&P absorbed into CSX Transportation 1991; Amtrak continues service today)
